text: The number one thing that should matter about a diss track and overall beef is who is forced to limp away in the end. It's like a chess move, where it can be difficult to judge a single move without knowing the end result. That said, I've enjoyed everything that's come out from both of them. I think that it's pulled the best out of Drake, and I believe he delivered with Push Ups, but knowing now how this thing has played out, it's a little more difficult to get hyped about Drake's wins during this fun period in hip hop. I love head nodders and old school, but I think that above all, hip hop is about telling a story. For me, a diss track is about stripping someone down through well constructed storytelling and wordcraft, executed with skill and flow. Good beat and production is a nice bonus, and is the kind of thing that can elevate it to diss rushmore status. Hopefully some of that made sense, haha. Cheers to a good rap feud!

text:
When dissecting Kendrick's 'Benjamin’s in my house’ bars it's like unraveling lyrics woven with hidden meanings, revealing artistry. As Kendrick himself implied, this diss to Drake is for those who fail the understand the hip-hop art and lyricism.

Kendrick integrates themes of art, money, and the stigma of snitching (He refers to Gunner’s situation about snitching on Young Thug on the rico case and that he believes Drake has done worse than Gunner)

Kendrick also continues  affirming his own stature as the GOAT “MJ”  (a title Drake claimed in "First Shooter")—a quadruple entendre, despite Drake's jest about his lyrical prowess.

With a reference to MJ‘S song 'Ben,' by “Artist” Michael Jackson Kendrick artistically associates Drake with both snitching and being a rat, and asserting himself with Art and his supremacy akin to Michael Jackson in the music realm. It's the play on words, where 'Ben' symbolizes the pet rat and Benjamin Franklin, whose likeness compares the face of the hundred-dollar bill, representing wealth.

In this lyrical showdown, Kendrick unquestionably destroys Drake, showcasing his musical genius and elevating his artistry to unmatched heights.


* Edited for context aimed at those who don’t actually understand the art of lyricism*
